name: Coagulation work-up to the rodenticide panel
rationale: Mucosal bleeding and haematuria with PT and APTT of 112 s: exclude anticoagulants, define the factor pattern (II, VII, IX, X low; V normal), give vitamin K, send an anticoagulant rodenticide panel and take the travel and food history. The case must show: normal platelets, fibrinogen and D-dimer; a correcting mixing study; a partial, unstable response to 10 mg vitamin K; the street-market food only on a specific question.

name: Liver disease from chronic hepatitis B
rationale: Chronic hepatitis B invites a hepatic coagulopathy. The case must show: normal factor V and fibrinogen, near-normal liver tests and albumin, no stigmata of chronic liver disease, suppressed hepatitis B on tenofovir and no cirrhosis on imaging; a liver biopsy while the INR is unmeasurable is a must-not-do.

name: A local bleeding source (gut, teeth or nose)
rationale: The care before admission (endoscopy, a dentist, tranexamic acid) looked for a local source. The case must show: no source at endoscopy, blood from the mouth, bleeding from several sites at once and no response to tranexamic acid.

name: Alcohol
rationale: The patient blames a night of drinking. The case must show: occasional drinking only, no alcohol in the blood, a normal MCV and near-normal GGT.

name: Haematuria from the urinary tract
rationale: Two days of visible haematuria. The case must show: isomorphic red cells without casts, sterile urine, normal renal function and normal renal tract imaging, and haematuria that clears once the clotting improves.

name: Other acquired or inherited coagulopathies (inhibitor, DIC, haemophilia, VWD)
rationale: A long APTT raises an inhibitor, DIC or a factor deficiency. The case must show: the mix corrects, normal thrombin time, fibrinogen, D-dimer and platelets, normal factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, no personal or family bleeding history; protein C and S low with the other vitamin K-dependent proteins.

name: Dietary or malabsorptive vitamin K deficiency
rationale: A diet of leftover meats with few vegetables. The case must show: no antibiotics, no diarrhoea or weight loss, normal coeliac serology and faecal elastase; diet alone does not explain factor levels this low or the incomplete response to vitamin K.

name: Deliberate or concealed ingestion
rationale: With no exposure the team considered self-harm or poisoning by another person. The case must show: no self-harm thoughts, no recreational drugs, a negative warfarin level and, on a specific question, a food source.

name: Autoimmune disease (sister with lupus)
rationale: A family history of lupus. The case must show: no rash, ulcers or joint symptoms, a negative ANA and anti-dsDNA, normal complement and no lupus anticoagulant.

name: Diabetes and its control
rationale: Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes. The case must show: hyperglycaemia, a raised HbA1c and diabetic dyslipidaemia that explain glycosuria, not the bleeding.

name: Dangerous bleeding (intracranial, gut)
rationale: An unmeasurable INR puts the brain at risk. The case must show: no headache, full consciousness, no retinal haemorrhage and a normal CT head; no melaena.

name: An infection picked up while travelling
rationale: Bleeding and haematuria after a trip abroad. The case must show: no fever, normal platelets and negative dengue, leptospira, scrub typhus and malaria tests and blood cultures.
